summary: Field-wise initializer that zeros a block at this+0x0 through this+0x88 and seeds two sentinel bytes (0x7C, 0x7E) with -1, then returns 0. No reads, no globals, no callees; it only stamps literals into a caller-provided object. Called by ArrayInitWithSentinelInLoop (00460C60), ClearPlayerSlots (00460CB0) and a thunk (00461470), so it is shared initialization state for a per-slot object.

local_names.this: object whose leading bytes up through the final field are being initialized

operations.description: Zero the leading dword at this+0x0
Zero the bytes at this+0x4, this+0x24, this+0x3C and this+0x5C
Seed sentinel bytes: this+0x7C set to -1, this+0x7D cleared to 0, this+0x7E set to -1
Zero the four word fields at this+0x80, this+0x82, this+0x84 and this+0x86
Return literal 0; the function is a pure initializer with no computed result, called by ArrayInitWithSentinelInLoop (00460C60), ClearPlayerSlots (00460CB0) and thunk 00461470

unresolved: The object type owning offsets 0x0-0x88 is unidentified; callers span an array initializer and a player-slot clearer, so it may be a shared per-slot state struct
Purpose of the -1 sentinels at this+0x7C and this+0x7E is not documented; they may be default handles or invalid-id markers
Why the final byte field is initialized but the bytes between the fifth byte field and the first sentinel are left untouched is unexplained
